summary: Firestore rules are highly secure and robust, with strict ownership checks, field-level restrictions on updates, input validation, and developer role verification.

findings.issue: There is no validation of fields during update on users/{uid} for the owner, allowing the owner to write invalid data types to their own profile, although it doesn't affect other users.
findings.recommendation: Add field type validation (is string, is int) for user profile updates by the owner.

findings.issue: No string length constraints or array size limits are enforced on posts/{postId} or users/{uid} collections, posing a minor resource exhaustion/DoS risk.
findings.recommendation: Implement size checks (e.g., resource.data.content.size() < 1000) for posts and user profile fields.

findings.issue: Type validation is missing for posts/{postId} fields (e.g. userId, createdAt, imageUrl) and user profile fields on creation.
findings.recommendation: Add basic type checks (e.g., request.resource.data.userId is string) in creation rules.
